incidents: Auto-sync/validator pre-commit hooks regenerate their own timestamped output (SKILLPACK-METADATA*, SKILLPACK-VALIDATION.md, SKILLPACK-RUNTIME-HEALTH.md, SKILLPACK-DEPENDENCY-GRAPH.md, dashboard.html, audit/COWORK-*) on every commit that touches nothing related to skills at all -- confirmed live today: 3 consecutive chore(sync) commits each triggered a fresh diff on the same 6-8 files. Not chased to convergence (would have committed indefinitely); stopped after 3 commits and flagged. This is the same set of files showing 9 touches each in this window's hotspot list -- a real bug, not incidental noise, and it inflates commit/LOC counts every week it goes unfixed.

trm-vault has NO git remote by design -- confirmed today via its pre-push hook, which hard-refuses any push and says explicitly not to bypass it. User asked to add a remote and push; hook blocked it; user chose to respect the guardrail and had the remote removed. Corrected in TODOS.md (was previously mischaracterized as a plain oversight) and logged to memory so it isn't re-litigated blind next time this comes up.

Backlog held flat at 10 open items despite 4 closes this period -- 4 new items opened at roughly the same rate items closed (Invoke-ToolforgeInstall node_modules copy bug, trm-vault remote reclassification, plus 2 from the prior week's schema/tsx gaps still open).
process_learnings: A guardrail hook that explicitly tells you not to work around it is a stronger signal than a TODOS.md line calling the same thing 'missing' -- worth testing the actual mechanism before trusting a backlog item's framing, especially one that's a week old.

Self-regenerating pre-commit output is a compounding cost: every unrelated commit this week paid a tax of 6-8 extra file diffs with no functional change. Left unfixed, next week's retro hotspot list will show the same files again for the same non-reason.
